title: Internal payment event processing redesign
problem_statement: Payment status change events (authorized, captured, refunded) are currently emitted directly from the payment service to three downstream consumers over point-to-point HTTP callbacks. Adding a new consumer requires a code change and redeploy of the payment service, and a slow or unavailable consumer can back up the payment service's own request handling.
proposed_solution: Publish payment status change events to a shared internal event bus that consumers subscribe to independently. The payment service publishes once per event and no longer calls consumers directly; the event bus retains events for 24 hours so a consumer that is briefly unavailable can catch up without the payment service resending anything.
constraints: Must reuse the existing internal event bus platform rather than introducing a new one.
Payment service publish latency must not regress beyond the current callback latency.
assumptions: All three current consumers can migrate to bus subscriptions within one release cycle.
The event bus already provides at-least-once delivery.
alternatives_considered: Keep direct callbacks but add a retry queue in front of each consumer.
Introduce a dedicated notification microservice that fans out to consumers on the payment service's behalf.
